findings.source_passage: How I snuffed that Tartar air!—how I spurned that turnpike earth!—that common highway all over dented with the marks of slavish heels and hoofs
findings.why_it_matters: The full exclamatory triple-beat construction—'How I snuffed that Tartar air!'—is Ishmael's voice at its most exuberant; the draft drops the first exclamation entirely and strips the 'slavish heels and hoofs' image, leaving only one-third of a signature rhetorical flourish.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'How I snuffed that Tartar air!—how I spurned that turnpike earth!—that common highway all over dented with the marks of slavish heels and hoofs' verbatim or very close before the sea-magnanimity sentence.

findings.source_passage: as though a white man were anything more dignified than a whitewashed negro
findings.why_it_matters: This aside carries significant interpretive weight on race and dignity; it is Melville's pointed ironic critique embedded in Ishmael's narration and has received sustained critical attention. The draft omits it entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the clause when describing the passengers' jeering at the pair's companionship.

findings.source_passage: Was there ever such unconsciousness? He did not seem to think that he at all deserved a medal from the Humane and Magnanimous Societies.
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical question 'Was there ever such unconsciousness?' and the ironic 'Humane and Magnanimous Societies' jest are Ishmael's narrator-voice at its most characteristic—admiring, gently satirical, philosophically charged. The draft jumps straight to the 'mutual joint-stock world' tag line, erasing the build-up that makes the final line land.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the lead-in: 'Was there ever such unconsciousness? He did not seem to think that he at all deserved a medal from the Humane and Magnanimous Societies. He only asked for water—fresh water—something to wipe the brine off' before the closing statement.

findings.source_passage: the Moss did homage to the blast; ducked and dived her bows as a slave before the Sultan
findings.source_locator: paragraph on open water / sailing passage
findings.why_it_matters: The slave/Sultan simile is a small but tonally distinctive Melvillean image; the draft's compressed sailing description omits it, mildly thinning the prose texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the simile when describing the Moss in the breeze: 'the Moss did homage to the blast; ducked and dived her bows as a slave before the Sultan.'

findings.source_passage: darted from the side with a long living arc of a leap
findings.why_it_matters: The draft says 'sprang a living arc' which preserves the image in compressed form; the phrase 'long' modifying the arc and the specific 'darted from the side' are slightly dimmed but the core survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor: restore 'darted from the side with a long living arc of a leap' for full rhythmic effect.

summary: Three medium-severity findings (the 'Tartar air' exclamatory trio cut to one beat, the 'whitewashed negro' ironic aside entirely absent, and the 'unconsciousness'/'Humane and Magnanimous Societies' lead-in erased) plus two low findings; none reach the single high-severity threshold, and three mediums are exactly the regeneration floor—verdict is a borderline pass, but the missing 'whitewashed negro' and 'unconsciousness' passages represent meaningful interpretive and voice losses that a regeneration pass should restore.
